Confirmed, with a necessary correction to the fix. Item 15 bundles the mapping property with a subvariety/quotient exactness theorem that neither R11.1 nor R11.5 states. The actual application is over a smooth complex curve (v3 p.29; published p.561). I read BLR §7.5 Propositions 2–3 and Proposition 3's proof, printed pp.186–187, in the public Arizona scan. Proposition 3(a) assumes the residue characteristic does not divide the complementary isogeny's degree; the closed immersion and smooth map with the specified kernel yield exactness under good reduction. Proposition 2 assumes residue characteristic zero for extending a closed immersion. Therefore the proposed new item must put the characteristic-zero residue-field hypothesis on the WHOLE exact-sequence assertion, or retain BLR's precise local prime-to-degree condition. It is wrong to assert unrestricted exactness first and restrict only the final closed-immersion clause. Separate unrestricted good reduction from this stronger assertion. Split the item, keep the R11 owner, and coordinate with Xie–Yuan without exporting the characteristic-zero theorem to characteristic p. Also avoid a dependency R11.5 -> R11.1: the existing forward chain R11.1 -> R11.2 -> R11.3 -> R11.4 -> R11.5 makes that cyclic. Use an independent earlier proof or a later derived node.

Confirmed. The three slips are absent from sourceIssues E1–E27, while the notes already identify two and item 40 silently restores equivariance. Published p.544 says endomorphism; the zero map contradicts the fibre-isomorphism requirement. The p.556 image has the unrestricted Hom intersection; Deligne Hodge II (4.1.3.2), p.43, explicitly requires a morphism of local systems. A constant E inside E times a non-isotrivial elliptic family supplies a counterexample to arbitrary fibre-map extension at a fibre isomorphic to E; the fixed-part inclusion actually used remains equivariant. The Ax references are inconsistent with the paper's own introduction and bibliography: [3] is the algebraic-group reference. Register the three slips with precise version-specific locators and actual correction searches. Grothendieck is [24] in v3 but [23] in the published bibliography, so do not copy that citation number verbatim across versions.

Rejected. The finding conflates two path requirements. The actual item 30 asks for a continuous definable path with semialgebraic first coordinates and a counted starting point; it does NOT impose analyticity on (0,1). Habegger–Pila's proof of Corollary 7.2 on v1 p.25 constructs exactly that version before its final reparametrization. Furthermore Gao–Habegger's special family admits an explicit repair of the coordinates after any reparametrization preserving y(0): by Corollary 7.2(iii), choose a counted (gamma', a') with y(0)=gamma'x-a', and replace gamma(s) by the constant gamma' and a(s) by gamma'x-y(s). The relation defining Z holds for all s; the path remains in GL_n(R) times R^n times X, and starts at gamma' in Gamma and a' in Z^n. It stays semialgebraic and is analytic whenever y is. In this family y is a fixed linear combination of the first coordinates, so Corollary 7.2(i) already gives its analyticity. Thus the observed loss of the original first coordinates does not establish an error in item 30 or a new gap in Lemma 5.2. The proposed alternative argument through gamma' is valid, but optional exposition does not warrant E31 as a confirmed source mistake. This comparison uses the public Habegger–Pila v1, not its unread published version.

Confirmed as partial library reuse. I read all three declarations at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. MeasureTheory.exists_pair_mem_lattice_not_disjoint_vadd (GeometryOfNumbers.lean:52) is a strict-volume, two-intersecting-translates theorem under a countable measurable action and invariant fundamental-domain measure. It is not the bounded measurable-set multiplicity conclusion used in published Proposition 7.2, p.575; the GN.1 contract/packet must still supply that deduction for nonconvex sets. IsDedekindDomain.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot (TorsionFree.lean:138) is the affine module input, not the scheme theorem or its dimension conclusion. NumberField.absLogHeight₁ (NumberField.lean:146, with absMulHeight₁:137) gives normalized algebraic-element height, hence the affine [1:x] portion of P^1 after comparison, not the complete projective height package. Add the citations as baselines, retain the full planned/missing statuses and owners, and describe the needed adapters explicitly.
